slots.title: US cash session — Aug. 28, 2026
slots.body:
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole appearance dominated the narrative into the close, with headlines describing a harder focus on inflation and interest-rate expectations. U.S. equity indexes finished softer rather than sharply broken, but the leadership underneath was narrow.

The S&P 500 closed at 7,711.76, down 0.2% (−19.23 points), after trading between 7,700.91 and 7,771.48.
The benchmark stayed below its 52-week high of 7,816.70 printed in the index data.

The Nasdaq Composite lost 0.5%, ending at 26,402.42 (−138.93), with a session range of 26,359.27 to 26,700.68.
Tech-heavy exposure showed up in the underperformance versus the Dow.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was nearly flat at 53,559.99, down less than 0.1% (−9.45 points).
That divergence mattered: large industrials did not match the pressure seen in growth and chip names.

Small caps took the largest index hit among the U.S. benchmarks in the feed.
The Russell 2000 fell 1.4% to 2,972.37, with the low of day matching the closing print at 2,972.37.

NVIDIA was the standout megacap mover by percentage among widely held names in the dataset, closing at 217.55, down 4.6% (−10.43).
Trading interest showed up in the actives list alongside the raw price decline.

Chip and semiconductor supply-chain peers moved in the same direction as NVIDIA on the close: Advanced Micro Devices finished at 465.58 (−2.3%), Taiwan Semiconductor at 417.52 (−2.3%), and ASML at 1,696.16 (−2.2%).

Apple bucked the weak Nasdaq tone, rising 1.6% to 319.70.
Meta Platforms gained 1.2% to 578.02, and Costco rose 1.2% to 945.47.
Tesla closed at 348.75, down 1.7%.

Financial megacaps were green on the session: Bank of America rose 1.9% to 62.32, and JPMorgan Chase gained 1.0% to 357.62.
Visa and Mastercard were up 0.5% and 0.6%, respectively.

Energy-linked large caps were modestly higher: Chevron closed at 201.88 (+1.1%), and Exxon Mobil at 156.70 (+0.2%).
Headlines also carried President Trump’s statements about a U.S.–Venezuela oil agreement; the tape showed Brent crude at 88.10, down 0.5%, and the U.S. Oil Fund (USO) at 129.70, down 0.2%.

Gold futures (GC) fell 2.9% to 4,529.90, a −134.10 move from the prior close of 4,664.00, with a session low of 4,495.00.
That sat alongside a firmer dollar read via the Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund (UUP) at 28.18, up 0.6%.

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-08-27) showed the 10-year at 4.7% and the 2s10s spread at 0.47 percentage points.
Bitcoin USD was quoted at 77,694.66, down 0.2% on the session.

The VIX closed at 14.43, down 0.6%, with an intraday band of 14.13 to 14.84.
Overseas indexes in the feed were mixed ahead of or outside the U.S. cash window, including the FTSE 100 up 0.3% and the Hang Seng down 0.3%.

The economic calendar flagged the Jackson Hole Symposium (high impact, U.S.) on 2026-08-29 in the data feed.
No earnings actuals were listed in the injected earnings calendar for this close.
